cards.title: Matrix-Specific Bioanalysis and Tissue Homogenate Concentration Normalization
cards.claim: Quantification across plasma or serum, bile, urine and tissue homogenates requires matrix-specific calibration and a documented analytical method. For tissue homogenates, retain tissue mass, added diluent and processing factors so an assay concentration can be related to the declared tissue concentration basis. Assays measuring chemical analyte and assays measuring antimicrobial activity are not interchangeable observations.
conditions: Several biological matrices or analytical methods contribute to one PK analysis.
Calibration, extraction recovery, selectivity and quantification limits are qualified for each analyte/matrix combination.
required_inputs: Analyte definition, matrix identity and assay method, including whether concentration is chemical or activity-derived.
Matrix-specific calibration range, LLOQ/ULOQ, recovery, precision and accuracy records.
Tissue wet mass, homogenization diluent/volume and subsequent dilution or concentration factors, with units.
Raw reported result and calculation showing the conversion to the stated final basis.
limitations: A validated method for one analyte/matrix does not validate another combination.
A tissue homogenate concentration is not an unbound extracellular or intracellular concentration.
The cited extraction protocol and numerical assay criteria are not universal defaults.
cards.downstream_use: Harmonize concentration units without losing the original matrix, assay or mass/volume basis before tissue/plasma comparison.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
